headline: MongoDB returns to profit as Atlas growth outruns costs
summary_short: MongoDB's FY2026 Q2 revenue rose 16.3% y/y to $687.6M, and the company swung to net income of $4.4M from a $47.0M loss a year ago as Atlas consumption growth (net ARR expansion rate 121%) lifted overall gross margin to 72%.
summary_long: Revenue grew 16.3% y/y to $687.6M, led by a $134.7M rise in subscription revenue as large existing customers expanded Atlas usage (net ARR expansion rate 121%). Overall gross margin rose to 72%, though subscription gross margin slipped to 75% on faster-growing Atlas infrastructure costs. Sales & marketing, R&D, and G&A expenses all rose on higher personnel, commissions, and software costs, but revenue growth outpaced them, narrowing the operating loss to $24.8M from $65.3M a year ago. Net income swung to $4.4M from a $47.0M loss, aided by $33.6M of gains on non-marketable securities. The company repurchased $100.0M of stock and held $2.4B in cash and short-term investments; remaining performance obligations stood at $1,458.6M. No forward guidance is disclosed.

Sales & marketing, R&D, and G&A expenses all rose on higher personnel, commissions, travel, and software costs, but revenue and gross-profit growth outpaced them, narrowing the operating loss.
